definitions.gloss: arrowroot starch; kudzu starch; kuzu powder
definitions.explanation: A fine white starch extracted from the root of the kudzu plant ({葛|くず}). Used as a thickener in Japanese cooking and as the base for traditional sweets. Prized for the smooth, glossy texture it gives to sauces and desserts.

examples.japanese: くず{粉|こ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦とろみ→とろみ：28703_toromi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。

examples.english: Dissolve the kuzu starch in water before adding it to the pot.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{仕上|しあ}がり→仕上がり：07432_shiagari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食感|しょっかん}→食感：06636_shokkan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧まったく⟦{違|ちが}う→違う：01957_chigau⟧。
examples.english: Pure kuzu starch is expensive, but the resulting texture is completely different.

notes:
The starch is extracted from the root of ⟦{葛|くず}→葛：28689_kuzu⟧ (kudzu/arrowroot vine, Pueraria montana). Written as くず{粉|こ} or {葛粉|くずこ}. The くず portion is often written in hiragana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- くず{粉|こ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{溶|と}く→溶く：26556_toku⟧: to dissolve kuzu starch (in water)
- {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ}: pure kudzu starch (100% kudzu, not blended)
- くず{粉|こ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦とろみ→とろみ：28703_toromi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to thicken with kuzu starch
- {吉野|よしの}くず: Yoshino kuzu — the most famous producing region

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{片栗粉|かたくりこ}→片栗粉：04923_katakuriko⟧: potato starch — the everyday thickening starch in Japanese kitchens; cheaper and more common
- コーンスターチ: cornstarch — another thickener, used mainly in Western-style cooking
- ⟦{葛|くず}→葛：28689_kuzu⟧: kudzu (the plant) — the source of the starch

CULTURAL NOTE:
くず{粉|こ} is essential for traditional ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧ (Japanese sweets) such as {葛切|くずき}り (kuzu noodles served chilled with brown sugar syrup), {葛餅|くずもち} (kuzu mochi), and {葛湯|くずゆ} (a warm, soothing drink made by dissolving kuzu starch in hot water, traditionally given to people with colds). {吉野|よしの} in {奈良県|ならけん} is the most renowned production area. True {本|ほん}くず{粉|こ} (pure kudzu starch) is expensive, so many commercial products are blends with {甘薯|かんしょ} (sweet potato) starch.
